To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

calcium overload in the heart causes a cyclosporine-sensitive mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT) in mitochondria isolated from rat hearts and that the MPT can be induced by calcium alone in isolated rat heart mitochondria.

calcium-induced cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction, as measured by the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, can be predominantly mediated by the opening of the cyclosporine (CsA)-dependent permeability transition pore (mPTP), and that this process is associated with a loss of mitochondrial matrix volume and the release of cytochrome c into the cytosol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying calcium-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in cardiac cells and its possible relationship to the mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT) pore.

the role of the mitochondrial permeability transition (PT) pore and the role of the calcium-dependent opening of the PT pore in the development of mitochondrial and cardiac dysfunction in heart failure.
the effects of calcium on the permeability of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of mitochondrial calcium in cell death and in the development of cardiac hypertrophy and failure remains controversial.
the calcium-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is predominantly caused by the opening of the cyclosporine a-sensitive mitochondrial permeability transition pores.

the calcium induced mitochondrial dysfunction is predominantly caused by the mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT) pore, which is a large non-selective pore that allows the passage of ions, small molecules, and even proteins across the mitochondrial inner membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

calcium-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is predominantly caused by cyclosporin A-dependent mitochondrial permeabilization, and that this process is mediated by cyclophilin D, which is an essential component of the mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT) pore.
calcium-induced cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death is predominantly mediated by a cyclosporine (CS)A-dependent mitochondrial permeability (PMT) transition pore (PTP).

we have shown that the Ca2+-induced mitochondrial permeability transition is the primary mechanism for mitochondrial dysfunction and that the cyclosporine-dependent pore is responsible for the majority of the mitochondrial dysfunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondria are a major player in the development of calcium overload-induced cardiac dysfunction.
the mitochondrial permeability transition (mPT) plays a key role in the pathogenesis of calcium (Ca2+)-induced cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction.

the mitochondrial permeability transition is a major factor that contributes to calcium-induced cardiac dysfunction, and that the cyclosporin A-dependent component of mitochondrial permeability transition contributes more to calcium-induced mitochondrial dysfunction than does the cyclosporine-independent component.
